name: Coffee Jelly

instructions.primary_message: In a small bowl, whisk granulated sugar, agar agar, and salt to combine.

In a small pot over medium-high heat, bring coffee to a boil. Reduce heat to medium-low. Add sugar mixture, whisking constantly and gently until fully dissolved, about 2 minutes. (To check if mixture has fully dissolved, run a spoon along bottom of the pot; there should be no sugar or agar agar adhering to the spoon.)

Pour mixture into an 8-by-8-inch baking pan. (To keep bubbles from forming, it's helpful to use a spouted ladle to slowly transfer the liquid into the pan.). Gently tap pan against the kitchen counter to eliminate any bubbles. Let cool sightly, until just warm to the touch, about 15 minutes.
Tighty cover pan with plastic wrap and refrigerate until cold and firm, at least 3 hours. (It will set within an hour, but should be chilled for the full 3 hours to ensure it is completely cold.)
Slice into 9 squares. Serve chilled, topping each piece with about 2 teaspoons heavy cream and a scoop of vanilla ice cream.

schema_metadata.keywords: coffee jelly, coffee jelly recipe, Japanese coffee jelly

description: In Japan, coffee is often in its jiggly, jellied dessert form. Made with black coffee to highlight the roasted, bitter flavors of the beans, Japanese coffee jelly is typically set with kanten (a type of agar-agar) or gelatin) and is served for dessert with heavy cream and ice cream.
notes:
Total time, including resting: 3 hr 30 min.

Optional or for serving: 1/3 cup heavy cream, divided, for serving; Vanilla ice cream, for serving

Notes: For the richest flavor, use coffee made with dark-roasted beans. In a pinch, instant espresso will also work.
Kanten agar-agar gives the coffee jelly a unique texture, but if you prefer a more Jello-like bounce, you can swap the kanten with 20 grams of unflavored gelatin powder. When dissolving the gelatin in the coffee, do not boil the coffee; heat the coffee on a stove until it’s steaming, then reduce heat to low and add gelatin. Gently stir and let sit until fully dissolved, about 2 minutes. Follow step 2 as listed, but to fully set the gelatin, cover and refrigerate for 5 hours or overnight.
author: Kiera Wright-Ruiz
